method: Rebuilt the selected credits and periods directly from the adopted Appendix 1 p. 21 and checked Articles 9.1, 11.4 and 12, then reread the 2026–2027 Study Guide course entries and independently checked current workbook offerings, gateway prerequisites and the evidence for the altered selections and retained combinations before comparing the resulting canonical record.
findings: 24 EC required track units, 12 EC required PPE in Practice, 24 EC restricted electives. Ethics II and International Trade are P4, History of Philosophy II and Global Justice P5. Three philosophy and one economics electives meet Article 11.4’s at-least-one-per-track rule and the annual plan’s two-per-period placement.

30 EC approved study abroad in P1–3, 6 EC qualitative methods and 6 EC tutorial in P4, 12 EC thesis in P5 and 6 EC PPE in Practice V in P6. The methods/policy alternative and internship/minor routes are excluded from this illustration.

OER 9.1 and thesis guide state 108 Year-1/2 EC by end of P3, with a 102 EC conditional route. Tutorial guide also prints 138 total EC and a separate 108 EC provisional threshold. The illustrated 120 Year-1/2 plus 30 study-abroad EC before P4 satisfies both ordinary thresholds. Thesis intent is registered in September. OER attendance and BSA conditions are non-credit. The thesis may use one or more PPE disciplines.

Public Economics substantively overlaps the market-failure and policy content of Governance for Society, with the latter’s transaction-cost approach and project remaining distinct. UCR Introduction to Political Philosophy aligns with VU’s normative Political Philosophy, while the experimental and empirical first-year political-science course remains unmatched.

Public Policy Analysis supplies concrete policy formulation and memo work. Behavioral Economics takes the fifth term in both economics routes. The revised political-economy route preserves all 24 courses. All three routes preserve two substantial disciplinary lines, with the third discipline at different weights and explicit limits on VU’s specialist courses and supervised research.
